For above every other sin, the wickedness of adultery is hated by God, because it not only destroys the person himself who sins, but those who eat and associate with him. For it is like the madness of a dog, because it has a nature of communicating its own madness.

**[34:57]** For the sake of chastity, therefore, let not only the elders, but even all hasten to accomplish marriage. For the sin of him who commits adultery necessarily comes upon all. Therefore, to urge the brethren to be chasteed is the first charity. For it is the healing of the soul for the nourishment of the body is rest. But if you love your brethren, take nothing from them, but share with them such things as you have. Feed the hungry. Give drink to the thirsty. Clothe the naked. Visit the sick so far as you can. Help those in prison. Receive strangers gladly into your own abodess. Hate no one. And how you must be pious. Your mind, your own mind will teach you judging rightly.

**[35:44]** But before all else, if indeed I need say it to you, come together frequently, if it were, every hour, especially on the appointed days of the meeting. For if you do this, you are within a wall of safety, for disorderliness is the beginning of predition. Let no one therefore forsake the assembly on the ground of envy toward a brother. For if any one of you forsake the assembly, he shall be regarded as those who scatter the church of Messiah and shall be cast out with adulterers. For as an adulterer under the influence of the spirit that is in him, he separates himself on some pretext and gives place to the wicked one against himself a sheep for the stealing as one found outside the fold. However, hear your bishop and do not weary of giving all honor to him, knowing that by showing it to him, it is born to Messiah, and from Messiah it is born to God, and to him who offers it is reququitted manifold.

**[36:39]** Honor therefore the throne of Messiah, for you are commanded even to honor the chair of Moses, and that although they who occupied are accounted sinners, and now I've said enough to you, I deem it superolous to say to him, how he is to live blamelessly since he is ano approved disciple of him who taught me also. But brethren, there are some things that you must not wait to hear, but must consider of yourself what is reasonable. Zakius alone, having given himself up wholly to labor for you, and needing s sustenance, and not being able to attend to his own affairs, how can he procure necessary support?

**[37:24]** Is it not reasonable that you are to take forethought for his living, not waiting for his asking you? For this is the part of a beggar. But he will rather die of hunger than submit to do this. And shall not you incur punishment for not considering that the workman is worthy of his hire. And let no one say, "Is then the word sold which was freely given." Far be it. For if anyone has the means of living and takes anything, he sells the word. But if he who has not takes support in order to live, as a master also took at supper among his friends, having nothing, though he alone is the owner of all things, he sends not. Therefore, suitably honor elders, catechist, useful deacons, widows who have been who have lived well, orphans as children of the church. But wherever there is need of any provision for an emergency, contribute altogether. Be kind one to another, not shrinking from the endurance of anything whatever for your own salvation.

**[38:26]** And having thus spoken, he placed his hand upon Zakius, saying, "Oh, you ruler, master of all, father and God, do you regard the shepherd with the flock. You are the cause. You are the power. We are that which is helped. You the helper, the physician, the savior, the wall, the life, the hope, the refuge, the joy, the expectation, the rest. In a word, you are all thanks to us. In order to the eternal attainment of salvation, you do cooperate, preserve, and protect. You can do all things, for you are ruler of rulers, lord of lords, governor of kings. Do you give power to the president to loose what ought to be loosed, to bind what ought to be bound? Do you make him wise? Do you as by his name protect the church of your Messiah as a fair bride? For thine etern eternal glory, praise the father and son, the holy ghost to all ages. Amen.

**[39:13]** And having thus spoken, he afterward said, "Whoever of you wish to be baptized, begin from tomorrow to fast, and to have hands laid upon you today by day, hands laid upon you day by day, and inquire after what matters to you, what matters you please. For I mean still to remain with you 10 days." And after having and after three days, having begun to baptize, he called me and Aquilla and Nitus, and said to us, "I'm going to set out for Ty after seven days. I wish you to go away this very day and to lodge secretly with Bernice the Canaanite, the daughter of Justa, and to learn from her and write accurately to me what Simon is about. For this is of great consequence to me that I may prepare myself accordingly. Therefore, depart straightway in peace.

**[39:57]** And leaving him baptizing as he commanded, we proceeded him to Tire of Phoenicia. All right. So, this uh completes book three. And when we come back, we'll uh pick it up in uh book four.
